text:
sophie: heads up — after last night's kernel + quant-profile flip we see a sharp drop in prefix cache warmup hit rate for chat routes. p50 ok but p99 latency up and costs spiking :grimacing:
lee: saw the alert, digging into perf dashboard now. which model family is most affected?
maria: mostly the 8k-context conversational models. baseline hit-rate ~82% -> dropped to ~48% on steady traffic.
sophie: exact numbers from prometheus: 
```
# query
avg_over_time(prefix_cache_hit_rate{route=~"/chat.*"}[30m])
# pre: 0.82, post: 0.48
```
dave: interesting — our canary rolled kernel variant K-v2 and quant profile qf-2 at ~4332070000. kernel selection policy also moved some requests to affinity scheduler that changes batching boundaries.
lee: i profiled a sample trace. warmup path shows key mismatches at canonicalization step — token normalization flip between tokenizer v1 and v2-ish? i dumped the raw input keys for two requests and hashes differ by padding bytes.
maria: screenshots? can you paste minimal dump?
lee: pasted below (redacted):
```
pref_key_v1: 0x7f9a3c... (len 128, pad=0x00)
pref_key_v2: 0x7f9a3c... (len 124, pad=0x20)
```
sophie: so keys semantically same but binary different -> cache miss. where did padding change happen? tokenizer update or kernel serialization layer?
dave: kernel K-v2 switched to new alignment-friendly memcpy in fused-attn path. that routine uses 32-byte alignment and can leave trailing garbage for small buffers. earlier we zeroed tail bytes. this explains the pad bytes.
maria: aha. quant profile qf-2 also changed how KV buffers are compacted (we moved to compressed int8 packing) which changed serialization length heuristics. combined effect -> key bit-rot.
lee: reproduction script attached (short):
```
# reproduce locally
./run_warmup_test --model chat-8k --kernel K-v2 --quant qf-2 --seed 42
```
results: cache_hit=0.46, p99=1.24s
sophie: mitigation options? immediate and medium term?
dave: immediate: flip node flag to force old memcpy path for hot routes (rollback K-v2 just for prefix path). quick but coarse.
maria: medium: canonicalize keys at serialization boundary — zero-pad or hash canonicalized token ids instead of raw buffer. cheaper: compute SHA1 of logical token sequence and use as key.
lee: also add a normalization layer in front of cache: strip trailing whitespace/pad and use deterministic encoder. cheap patch maybe <1 day.
infra-bot: deploy job queued: rollback-kernel-prefetch-flag to staging. ETA 20m.
sophie: let's do quick rollback for prod hotfix while we land canonicalization PR. dave, can you submit rollback?
dave: submitting now. will monitor hit-rate and cost.
maria: i'll start canonicalization PR and add unit tests that fuzz padding and alignment. also add perf test to ensure hash path doesn't regress p50.
sophie: thx. action items:
- dave: rollback kernel flag for prefix warmup (done and monitor)
- maria: canonicalization PR + fuzz tests (wip)
- lee: end-to-end synthetic run and compare pre/post metrics, include flame graphs for NVidia profiler
- sophie: coordinate postmortem and customer comms if SLA impacted

lee: note — longer-term: batching heuristics change in K-v2 also moved batching window from 16ms -> 10ms which reduces opportunity for continuous batching; that likely lowered effective cache priming. we should evaluate tradeoffs before re-enabling.
sophie: agreed. include batching window A/B in rollout checklist.
lee: will add.
maria: initial telemetry after rollback: hit-rate creeping back to 78% within 12m, p99 improving. will post full graphs in #eng-runtime once stable. :thumbsup:
